title: R_5(3(x-y)=1z) > 243: the a^k law fails at five colours
statement: The 5-colour Rado number of 3(x-y) = 1z is strictly greater than 243 = 3^5: there is a 5-colouring of {1,...,243} with no monochromatic solution. Consequently the natural generalisation of Chang-De Loera-Wesley's Theorem 1.2(3) -- that R_k(a(x-y)=bz) = a^k whenever gcd(a,b)=1 and a >= b+2, for every k >= 3 -- is FALSE. It holds at k=3 (R_3 = 27, ledger claim rado-r3-a3-b1) and at k=4 (R_4 = 81, ledger claim rado-r4-a3-b1, CDLW Table 10) and fails at k=5. The exact value of R_5(3(x-y)=1z) is not known.

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022 / arXiv:2210.03262
prior_art.establishes: Theorem 1.2(3): R_3(a(x-y)=bz) = a^3 for b >= 1, a >= b+2, gcd(a,b)=1. Lemma 4.1: R_k(a(x-y)=bz) >= a^k for every k, by the a-adic valuation colouring. Table 10: R_4(3(x-y)=z) = 81. The paper contains NO k=5 value and NO k=5 upper bound for any member of this family; verified by reading the rendered v1 PDF (its compiled form does contain Tables 9-15, unlike the arXiv source tarball).

prior_art.citation: A. C. Li, 'On Rado Numbers for x+by=bz: The b^k Pattern and a Threshold Conjecture', SSRN 6814341 (posted 2026-06-03)
prior_art.establishes: REPORTEDLY: R_5(3) > 296 > 243 with an explicit 5-colouring, and the conjecture R_k(b) = b^k iff k <= 2(b-1). NOT VERIFIED HERE: SSRN returns HTTP 403 to every fetch attempted, so these are search-engine summaries of the abstract page, not directly read text. The family identification IS verified: x + by = bz rearranges to x = b(z-y), a permutation of coordinates, so it induces the same 3-uniform hypergraph on [n] as b(x-y) = 1z; checked as sets-of-sets for b = 1..7 and n in {1,2,5,13,40,97,200}, 49/49 identical. If the report is accurate then our 243 result is a WEAKER independent reproduction of it and is not new; what is ours is that it is certified end to end with no external solver or checker.

evidence.supports: R_5 > 243 (lower bound; 243 = 3^5, so this refutes R_5 = a^k)
evidence.notes: A 5-colouring of [243] using all five colours, no monochromatic solution among the 16,362 solutions of 3(x-y)=z in [243]^3. Class sizes {1:63, 2:54, 3:41, 4:28, 5:57}. Decoded from cell 137 of the cube cover and verified four independent ways. STRUCTURE, recorded because it explains why the search was needed: colour 2 is EXACTLY the valuation stratum {j : v_3(j) = 1} (all 54 of it) while the other four classes partition {v_3 = 0} u {v_3 >= 2} into interval-like shells. The pure valuation colouring provably cannot be extended to 243 -- joining 243 to class v=0 makes {82,1,243} monochromatic, to v=1 makes {84,3,243}, to v=2 makes {90,9,243}, to v=3 makes {108,27,243}, to v=4 makes {162,81,243} -- so the extremal object at k=5 is structurally unlike the construction that is extremal at k=3 and k=4.

known: R_5(3(x-y)=1z) > 243, witnessed and verified (evidence row witness-243). This is the whole content of the claim: the a^k prediction is refuted, the true value is unknown.
R_3(3(x-y)=1z) = 27 = 3^3 (ledger claim rado-r3-a3-b1) and R_4(3(x-y)=1z) = 81 = 3^4 (ledger claim rado-r4-a3-b1, CDLW Table 10), so the law holds at k=3 and k=4 and fails at k=5.
Lemma 4.1's lower bound R_k >= a^k remains SOUND at k=5 -- a lower bound cannot be refuted by exhibiting a larger colouring. What fails is its tightness.

Corroborating but UNVERIFIED: Li (SSRN 6814341) reportedly gives R_5(3) > 296 and conjectures the law holds exactly for k <= 2(a-1), which for a=3 means k <= 4. Our data (27, 81, and >243 at k=5) is consistent with that threshold at every point we have.

Incremental climbing from the 243 witness reached a verified 5-colouring of [251] and stalled at 252 across four seeds; that is a search limit, not a threshold, and the intermediate witnesses are not shipped.
frontier.would_settle: A verified 5-colouring of [n-1] together with an exhaustive checked refutation of F_n, for the same n. Both artifact kinds and their checkers exist in this family. The obstruction is the refutation side at five colours, which has never been done at any n for any member of this family.
frontier.attack_notes: The satisfiable side is not free here: the a-adic construction that settles every n <= a^k - 1 in milliseconds provably cannot reach a^k, and min-conflicts warm-started from it failed three times. What worked was cube-and-conquer, which starts from no construction at all (35.8 s). Monolithic proof-producing CDCL is the wrong tool on the satisfiable side of this instance: it emitted 2.6 GB of DRAT in 8 minutes without deciding, and its resident set tracked the proof size almost exactly, so on a 26 GiB host it would have OOM-killed before answering.

notes: Recorded because a refuted prediction is evidence. This claim exists to stop the a^k law being quoted beyond k=4: the conjecture was the headline target of this campaign lane and the machinery falsified it in 36 seconds. See also rado-r5-a3-b2-frontier, which recorded the analogous non-tightness of this project's own shell bound at k=5 -- two independent constructions, both extremal at k=3 and k=4, both non-extremal at k=5.
